WF-03 Step 5 -- close ISS-0200. You produced this run's diagnosis at Step 1; the closing REVIEWER gate PASSED both your NO-CHANGE verdict and the edit recording it, after one rework. Read handoffs/WF03-ISS0200-20260821/step-03c-reviewer-regate.json before starting -- it PASSES the run and then names three MINORs, two of which it says must be acted on BEFORE this step writes anything. They are not restated here.

ISS-0200 BECOMES THE FIRST RECORD IN THIS PROJECT EVER TO CARRY `status: no_defect`. Everything you write is the precedent every later no-defect record copies. A first use that does not meet its own new bar would be the worst possible precedent for it -- DOC-UPDATER flagged exactly this at Step 3 and it is the main risk of this step.

(1) WRITE docs/issues/ISS-0200.yaml TO THE BAR ITSELF. The four-item evidence bar is in docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md's "Issue status vocabulary" -- read it there and satisfy it item by item, in the record. Bar item 1 forbids inherited figures BY NAME, so the figures in the record must be the ones you measured, not the ones ISS-0200's own filing asserted; where your measurement and the filing differ, the record says so (your Step 1 result corrected the 2.1x generalisation UPWARD to 2.92x pooled -- that correction belongs in the record, not just in a handoff). Cite handoffs/WF03-ISS0200-20260821/step-005-01-diagnose.json by path for the full working. Item 2 wants the candidate mechanisms named individually INCLUDING the ones the data did not support -- that list is the part an uninvestigated issue could never fabricate, which is why the bar demands it. Item 3 wants the method's stated limitations: your own shingle-calibration caveat, and the re-gate's finding that the least-dense-file identity is metric-dependent. Do not soften either; a negative result that hides the weakness of the test that produced it is worth less than no record at all.

(2) THREE ONE-LINE DOC CORRECTIONS THE RE-GATE NAMED. ORCH rules all three in scope for this step -- two because the gate says they must land before this record is written, the third because it is a factual inaccuracy this run introduced into a canonical document and it is two words.

  (a) KEY-NAME COLLISION. ORCH RULES: rename the pair to `verdict_in_run:` / `verdict_at:` in ISSUE_QUEUE.md, rather than the gate's other option of keeping `closed_*` at top level with a stated meaning. Reasons, so you can overturn this if you find it wrong rather than merely comply: `closed_at` already means "when GitHub closed the issue" at ISS-0109.yaml:314, and a registry ISS-0191's linter is meant to read mechanically should not carry one key with two meanings distinguished only by nesting depth; `verdict_*` is self-describing and cannot collide with a GitHub close at any nesting level; and no record uses it yet, so the rename costs one line now and a sweep later. If you disagree, say so in result.issues and state what you did -- HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 1.1 governs, and a verified disagreement outranks this dispatch. Whichever pair you land on, ISS-0200 must then USE it, and the record should make plain what the timestamp measures.

  (b) WF-03 STEP 5's OWN PSEUDOCODE. Two parts in docs/agents/workflows/WF-03_issue_resolving.md, both in the block you are executing right now, which is why they are yours. Item 1's template still opens with a concrete copyable `status: resolved` line; make the template name the alternatives so a weak model copying line one cannot land on the wrong status. Item 2 hardcodes a GitHub close comment reading "Fixed in <run-id>... and the regression test at <path>" -- on a no-defect close that publishes a false resolution claim to an external audience and cites a regression test this run does not have. Make item 2 branch on the status.

  (c) THE ISS-0202 GLOSS. HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's new parenthetical glosses ISS-0202 as measuring handoffs whose artifacts_out names ONLY their own file; ISS-0202 measured the broader "lists their own handoff file as one of their outputs". Correct the gloss to match what ISS-0202 actually says. Do not add a figure -- the re-gate specifically confirmed no number is smuggled back in under the citation, and that must stay true.

(3) CLOSE THE GITHUB ISSUE, #391, per WF-03 Step 5 item 2 -- but write the comment yourself under (2)(b)'s corrected form. It must not claim a fix, must not cite a regression test, and must state plainly that the issue was investigated and measured to carry no defect, pointing at docs/issues/ISS-0200.yaml and the diagnosis handoff. This comment is the one artefact an outside reader sees without following a pointer, so it carries the same honesty burden the record does.

DO NOT: reopen the NO-CHANGE verdict or anything else this run's gates certified; touch HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 4 or section 2's four worked examples (ISS-0200 AC4 protects them and they have now been certified byte-identical twice); re-edit ISS-0191.yaml or the H-SIZE-3 Enforcement extension; or absorb the sha-recording finding, which is filed as ISS-0205.

Re-verify AC4 byte-identity after your edits and quote it, exactly as Step 3 did -- you are touching the same file and this is the third time that span has needed protecting. Commit by explicit filename. ORCH runs a short closing gate on this step before Step Final, so state your evidence in a form a validator can re-derive.

result.summary:
WF-03 Step 5 -- ISS-0200 CLOSED as `no_defect`, the first record in this project to carry that status. All nine acceptance criteria met. ORCH's key-pair ruling APPLIED, not overturned (reasoning below). GH#391 closed with a comment that claims no fix. ISS-0200 AC4 re-verified post-edit and byte-identical.

=== (1) docs/issues/ISS-0200.yaml -- WRITTEN TO THE BAR, ITEM BY ITEM ===

The record now carries `status: no_defect`, `verdict_in_run: WF03-ISS0200-20260821`, `verdict_at: "2026-08-21T10:34:11Z"` (clock, not memory), and four evidence blocks keyed so a reader can check them against ISSUE_QUEUE.md's bar one at a time: `evidence_1_first_hand_measurement`, `correction_to_this_issues_own_figures`, `evidence_2_candidate_mechanisms`, `evidence_3_method_limitations`. The record parses: `yaml.safe_load` returns status `no_defect` and 24 top-level keys.

BAR ITEM 1 -- FIRST-HAND MEASUREMENT, NO INHERITED FIGURES. The producing loop is quoted verbatim in the record (the script lived in git-ignored `scratch/`, so it is quoted rather than committed). The corpus figures are the ones I measured at Step 1: 605 parseable files / 60 run directories / 0 unparseable; summary median 2,986, p90 8,493, p95 12,323, max 47,036, total 2,599,136; description median 704, p90 3,940, p95 5,737, max 19,040, total 889,118; per-handoff ratio median 3.53x, p90 13.86x, max 43.5x; 120 of 605 summaries (19.8%) over 6,000 chars against 26 of 605 descriptions (4.3%). Every one of these is a Step 1 measurement, and the record says so explicitly. Nothing is inherited from the filing, which bar item 1 forbids by name. The record cites `handoffs/WF03-ISS0200-20260821/step-005-01-diagnose.json` by path for the full working, and the two REVIEWER gates by path.

BAR ITEM 1's DISAGREEMENT CLAUSE -- THE 2.1x CORRECTION IS NOW IN THE RECORD, NOT ONLY IN A HANDOFF. `correction_to_this_issues_own_figures` states that all eleven of the filing's specific figures re-derived exactly, and that the ONE correction runs UPWARD: "2.1x" is one run's ratio (143,465/68,348 = 2.099x on WF03-ISS0117-20260821) which the title generalises to the corpus, while pooled corpus-wide the gap is 2,599,136 / 889,118 = 2.92x over 605 files. The record states in terms that the generalisation understated the effect it asserted, and why this belongs in the file: a later reader citing "2.1x" from this record as a corpus figure would be citing a number this run superseded.

BAR ITEM 2 -- ALL SIX MECHANISMS NAMED INDIVIDUALLY, INCLUDING THE UNSUPPORTED ONES (which is all six). M1 artifacts_out restatement (n=35, median 0.059, max 0.264; and only 46/120 large summaries name an artifacts_out basename at all, against 20/20 on the dispatch side, so the structural screen does not even select); M2 own issues[] in prose (n=130, median 0.009, max 0.162); M3 validator restating producer (n=248, median 0.002, max 0.200 -- flagged in the record as the load-bearing negative, direct positive evidence that section 4's re-derivation requirement is honoured rather than echoed); M5 echoing task.description (n=120, median 0.002, max 0.069); M6 restating an earlier summary in the same run (n=100, median 0.007, max 0.162); M7 restating a named artifacts_in file (n=119, median 0.018, max 0.264). None of the 120 exceeded 0.30 on any axis. The record states plainly that the labels are the diagnosis handoff's own and that no M4 row was reported -- an unused label, not a suppressed result -- so the gap cannot be read as a hidden negative. The two independent lines (evidence density; the hand-read of the hardest case) and the asymmetry argument are recorded with them.

BAR ITEM 3 -- LIMITATIONS, UNSOFTENED, BOTH OF THEM. (i) The shingle calibration: against the 26 large DISPATCHES -- the side where a defect IS known to exist -- the same 8-gram method gives median 0.054, p90 0.200, max 0.347, so it barely separates the side already proven guilty, because ISS-0198's cite-and-restate was paraphrase and verbatim shingles are under-powered against paraphrase. The record states in terms that M1-M7 are WEAK EVIDENCE TAKEN ALONE and load-bearing only comparatively, and that a paraphrase-tolerant method could find something this one cannot. (ii) The re-gate's finding: a variant density metric reproduces the direction with different absolute values AND a different least-dense file, so the hardest-case identity is a property of the metric, not a fact about the corpus; the record forbids citing 65.3%/36.7% as exact without restating the metric. (iii) I added a third: this is a point-in-time result about a mechanism, not a guarantee one cannot appear later -- which is the standing justification for the reporting-only linter extension. Neither of the two required limitations is softened; both are stated as weaknesses of the test, in the same paragraph as the result they weaken.

BAR ITEM 4 -- see (2)(a).

=== (2)(a) THE KEY PAIR: ORCH'S RULING APPLIED, NOT OVERTURNED ===

I checked the ruling rather than complying with it, as the dispatch asked. I confirmed first-hand that `closed_at:` already exists in the registry with a different meaning -- `grep -n closed_at docs/issues/ISS-0109.yaml` -> line 314, `closed_at: "2026-08-21T03:18:27Z"` nested under `resolution:`, and that record's own prose attributes it to `gh issue view 358 --json state,closedAt`, i.e. GitHub's close event. `grep -rn "closed_in_run\|verdict_in_run" docs/` returned three hits, all rule text (ISSUE_QUEUE.md:226, WF-03:163, WF-03:176) and ZERO records, so the rename costs one line now and a sweep never. ORCH's reasoning holds and I APPLIED it: ISSUE_QUEUE.md bar item 4 now mandates `verdict_in_run:` / `verdict_at:`, and states BOTH exclusions -- not `resolved_*` (asserts a resolution that did not happen) and not `closed_*` (already means the GitHub close, and one key with two meanings distinguished only by nesting depth is not readable by the mechanical linter ISS-0191 specifies). No disagreement to record under HANDOFF_PROTOCOL section 1.1.

ISS-0200 USES the settled pair, and the record makes plain what the timestamp measures: `verdict_keys_note` states that `verdict_at:` is when THIS RUN reached its verdict, not when GitHub closed the issue, and gives the reason. `github_close_note` then records GitHub's own closedAt, 2026-08-21T10:36:34Z, alongside it -- the two events are two minutes apart and now visibly distinct in the first record that could have conflated them.

=== (2)(b) WF-03 STEP 5's OWN PSEUDOCODE, BOTH PARTS ===

Item 1's template line no longer leads with a concrete wrong status. It now reads `status: <resolved | instrumented | no_defect>, plus THAT status's own key pair and its own required evidence`, followed by the per-status key mapping (resolved -> resolved_*; instrumented -> resolved_* plus a required superseded_by:; no_defect -> verdict_*, never resolved_*) and the imperative to check against ISSUE_QUEUE.md BEFORE writing the line. A weak model copying line one now copies a placeholder it cannot mistake for an answer, where before it would have copied `status: resolved`. The failure mode is removed, not corrected after the fact.

Item 2 now BRANCHES ON THE STATUS. The hardcoded "Fixed in <run-id> ... and the regression test at <path>" survives only under the `resolved` branch; `instrumented` gets a comment that names the shipped work and the successor issue and states the root cause is NOT removed; `no_defect` gets a comment that states investigated-and-measured, no defect, nothing changed, no fix, no regression test, pointing at the issue file and the diagnosis handoff. The block closes with "Never claim a fix or cite a regression test on a non-`resolved` close." WF-03's deference to ISSUE_QUEUE.md is untouched -- the vocabulary is still not restated there, and the prose sentence naming `no_defect`'s keys was updated to `verdict_in_run:`/`verdict_at:` for consistency (line 176).

=== (2)(c) THE ISS-0202 GLOSS ===

HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's parenthetical now reads "handoffs that list their own handoff file among their outputs", matching ISS-0202.yaml:13's actual measurement ("190 of the 449 handoffs carrying a non-empty `result.artifacts_out` list THEIR OWN handoff file AS ONE OF THEIR OUTPUTS"). NO FIGURE WAS ADDED -- the parenthetical still quotes no number, so nothing is smuggled back in under the citation and the re-gate's finding on that point stays true. One adjacent line was re-wrapped so the paragraph stays inside the file's width; no other word changed.

=== (3) GH#391 CLOSED ===

Command: `gh issue close 391 --comment "..."`. Output, verbatim:
    ✓ Closed issue tvolodi/letflow#391 (ISS-0200: result.summary has no size discipline, and it is the larger half of the artefact)
Verified independently: `gh issue view 391 --json state,closedAt` -> {"state":"CLOSED","closedAt":"2026-08-21T10:36:34Z"}.

The comment, in full:
---
Investigated and measured in run WF03-ISS0200-20260821; no defect found and nothing was changed. No fix was made and there is no regression test.

The question was whether `result.summary` carries a redundancy defect distinct from being genuinely long. Measured first-hand over 605 handoff files across 60 runs; six candidate restatement mechanisms were tested individually and none was supported (not one of the 120 large summaries exceeded 0.30 shingle overlap on any axis). The premise that summaries are the larger half is confirmed and in fact understated -- 2.92x pooled, not the 2.1x this issue filed -- but size here is bought by first-hand attestation, not by duplication. Closed as `no_defect`, which asserts that the alleged defect was checked for and measured to be absent; it does not assert that anything was fixed.

The method's limitations, including where the test is under-powered, are stated in the record rather than omitted.

Record: docs/issues/ISS-0200.yaml
Full working, producing code and figures: handoffs/WF03-ISS0200-20260821/step-005-01-diagnose.json
---
It claims no fix, cites no regression test, states the no-defect outcome plainly, names what `no_defect` does and does not assert, and points at both artefacts. It also carries the corrected 2.92x rather than the filed 2.1x, so the external record does not contradict the internal one.

=== ISS-0200 AC4 RE-VERIFIED POST-EDIT ===

    `git diff --numstat 7322185 -- docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md` -> `80  0` (unchanged from 03c: my edit re-worded two lines that are themselves part of the inserted block, so it adds no net line)

=== SCOPE AND FILES ===

Four files changed, all four in this handoff's `owned_modules`. I did NOT reopen the NO-CHANGE verdict or anything else this run's gates certified, did not touch HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 4 or section 2's worked examples (proved above, not asserted), did not re-edit ISS-0191.yaml or the H-SIZE-3 Enforcement extension, and did not absorb the sha-recording finding, which stays filed as ISS-0205.

I verified the ruling's two factual premises first-hand rather than accepting them: `closed_at:` does already exist at docs/issues/ISS-0109.yaml:314 with the GitHub-close meaning (that record's own prose attributes it to `gh issue view 358 --json state,closedAt`), and `grep -rn "closed_in_run\\|verdict_in_run" docs/` returns three hits, all rule text and zero records, so no sweep is owed. The rename to `verdict_in_run:`/`verdict_at:` is in force in ISSUE_QUEUE.md and in WF-03, and ISS-0200 uses it. RESIDUAL for a later run, not actionable here: ISS-0109 is an `instrumented` record carrying `resolved_in_run:`, which the vocabulary now says asserts a resolution that record did not perform. That is a pre-existing record under a rule written after it, outside this run's scope and not touched.

ISSUE_QUEUE.md's own worked example for ISS-0200 (added earlier in this run, in the section I edited) is now the one place in the registry that summarises this verdict WITHOUT the four-item bar behind it -- it quotes 605 files, 60 runs and six mechanisms in two sentences. Its figures are correct and match what I measured, so nothing false is asserted and this did not need fixing here. Flagged only because it is the shape a later no-defect record might copy INSTEAD of the full record: the worked example is an index entry, and ISSUE_QUEUE.md's bar requires the evidence to live in the ISSUE FILE. If a future run's record looks like the worked example rather than like docs/issues/ISS-0200.yaml, it has not met the bar. Worth a one-line note in the vocabulary section at some later run; not worth reopening a section this run's gates already certified.
